newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE - REAL BETIS PENPIX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE - REAL BETIS PENPIX.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to be in the Real Betis squad against Barcelona in the Spanish Cup final on Saturday:
Toni Prats. Goalkeeper. 25. Former Spanish junior international who joined from Celta last summer. Solid rather than spectacular but only let in 44 goals last season.

Pedro Jaro. Goalkeeper. 34. Former Real Madrid player who joined Betis four years ago. Lost form dramatically during 1995-96 season which led to the signing of Prats, and Jaro has been his understudy ever since.
Jaime Quesada. Defender. 25. Right back who once made the headlines by scoring the winning goal for lowly Lleida against Barcelona in the Camp Nou. Mainly on the bench last season.
Hristo Vidakovic. Defender. 28. Bosnian-born but now a Yugoslav international. Reputation as a hard-tacking central defender or libero.
Roberto Rios. Defender. 25. Son of former international Eusebio Rios. Usually plays on the right side of the defence and made his Spanish international debut last October.
Tomas Olias. Defender/midfielder. 28. Late developer. Joined Betis in 1993 after spells with various lower division clubs. Usually plays down the right side.
Juan Urena. Defender. 29. A survivor from their last bout of second division football. Missed most of the 1995-96 season through injury and has spent a lot of time on the bench this year.
Juan Merino. Midfielder. 26. Former reserve team defender who has found more success on the left side of the midfield and been first choice for most of the season.

Alexis Trujillo. Midfielder. 31. Club captain and penalty taker. Skillful midfielder and good at providing crosses to the Betis strikers. Joined Betis two years ago from Tenerife. Scored vital away goal against Celta in Cup semifinal.
Juan Canas. Midfielder. 25. Disciplined and hard working. Product of the Betis youith system but failed to hold down a regular place last season.
Albert Nadj. Midfielder. 22. Yugoslav international. A tireless worker down the right side but struggled with injuries last season. Primarily a backup to Finidi George.
Nenad Bjelica. Midfielder. 25. Croatian left-footer. Covers for Robert Jarni. Scored the Betis goal in the home leg of the semifinal against Celta.
Robert Jarni. Midfielder/striker. 28. Spells with various Italian clubs before moving to Betis two years ago. Croatian international. Former wing-back who moved into the midfield.
Excellent crosser of the ball and dangerous at free kicks.

Finidi George. Midfielder/striker. 26. Nigerian international signed from Ajax last summer. Operates mainly down the right side and made an immediate impact. Very quick and skilful and as a result has suffered many indiscriminate tackles. Recently had knee ligament problems.

Alfonso Munoz. Striker. 25. Second highest scorer in the Spanish first division with 25 goals last season. Spanish international who started out life as a goalkeeper. White boots and extravagant goal celebrations are his trade marks Peir Cherubino. Striker. 26. Usually Alfonso's partner up front. Born in Rome but moved to Spain as a child when his father decided to set up a fencing school. Top scorer for Betis in 1995-96 season with 14 goals.

Wojciech Kowalczck. Striker. 25. Made his name in the Polish team at the 1992 Olympics. Signed from Legia Warsaw in 1994 for a then club record 400 million pesetas ($2.84 million) but struggled to hold down a regular place until recently.

Juan Sabas. Striker. 30. Prodigy who never quite fulfilled his early promise with Athletico Madrid. Joined Betis in 1994 and now mainly used as an effective substitute who has turned round several games this season.
